author: Pedro Vilela
title: Aula da cadeira
content:
Tudo em que dá pra sentar é cadeira! — berrou Jorginho, de doze anos.
	Faz um tempo que dou aulas de matemática extracurricular para pré-adolescentes e gosto sempre de alterar o material, já que não preciso seguir nenhum programa de conteúdo muito rígido. Recentemente pensei que seria interessante tentar ensiná-los a importância (e a dificuldade) de boas definições e, antes de lhes apresentar as bases euclidianas do fazer matemático, propus um desafio a fim de mostrar que essa empreitada é muito mais complicada do que o pai da geometria fez parecer. Expliquei que a matemática moderna é feita a partir de definições muito precisas, que delimitam exatamente os objetos que querem — bem — definir, mas que, ao longo de sua vasta história, houve inúmeros embates sobre como deveria ser definido, por exemplo, um plano. Antes, porém, de entrar de fato nos objetos abstratos da mãe das ciências, sugeri que começássemos por delimitar algo mais concreto, mais empolgante.


— Alguém pode me dizer o que é uma cadeira?


— Tem um encosto, quatro pernas e dá pra sentar! — alguém no fundo falou.


— E se o encosto quebrasse, ainda seria uma cadeira? — perguntei, crente de que eu conduziria essa investigação magistralmente, pelo infalível método socrático.


— Aí seria uma cadeira quebrada, professor! — Começaram a rir.


— Pois bem, eu quero uma lista de características que a cadeira PRECISA ter para ser uma cadeira. Se ela não precisa de encosto, a lista também não precisa.


— Lá em casa tem uma que não tem apoio de braço, nem encosto, nem perna! É um quadradão assim, e a gente chama de cadeira.


— Quadrado, não. Cubo. — disse Jorginho.


— Certo, então é só um objeto em que dá pra sentar. Seria isso? — perguntei.


— Não! — exclamou Gabriel. — Dá pra sentar no chão, mas o chão não é uma cadeira.


— O chão não é objeto!


— Tá, mas dá pra sentar numa mesa também, e mesa não é cadeira!


Os alunos engataram na discussão e me segurei para deixá-los livres, queria ver se chegariam a algum consenso. Continuaram se lançando exemplos e contraexemplos até que a turma se dividiu em dois grupos: um deles, liderado por Jorginho (que tem uma incrível memória, sempre me lembra de fazer a chamada), defendia que tudo em que se podia se sentar poderia ser chamado de cadeira; o outro grupo, cuja voz mais ardente vinha de Gabriel, tinha como fundamento a intenção do criador do objeto: se alguém fez algo em que se poderia se sentar e o batizou de cadeira, logo aquilo assim seria chamado. As duas escolas de pensamento, então, travaram um feroz embate acerca da natureza real de um tronco cortado na floresta.


Fiquei tão absorvido pelo debate, pela truculência com que sustentavam suas alegações, que me esqueci de que esse é um problema sem solução. A impossibilidade de um consenso foi se tornando mais clara quando vi alguns alunos subindo em suas cadeiras como demonstração de um argumento que não captei por completo e vi bolas de papel voando em suas direções, certamente carregadas de eloquentes réplicas. Tive que me restabelecer como autoridade daquela ágora vulcânica assim que começaram os gritos de “DERRUBA! DERRUBA!”.


— Chega! — e dei um tapão na lousa tentando disfarçar minha satisfação em ter instigado um bélico debate filosófico entre pré-adolescentes.


Mas no silêncio borbulhante da turma ainda com os peitos ebulindo opiniões, Gabriel se levantou lenta e confiantemente e, com uma folha de papel amassada na mão, foi em direção à lata de lixo, gesto que passou despercebido pelos rivais. Eu o olhava pacientemente, esperando-o voltar a sua carteira para que eu pudesse prosseguir com a aula. Ele jogou fora o papel e, no caminho de volta ao seu assento, foi para o palanque na frente da sala, levantou os braços e disse “Tá aqui a cadeira do Jorginho!” e encheu a mão com o argumento que tinha entre as pernas.

author: Gabriel Barros
title: Moraes deve ser investigado, Mendonça, afastado e relatórios são ilegais, diz professor
content:
A divulgação, permitida pelo ministro André Mendonça, de um relatório da Polícia Federal (PF) contendo mensagens enviadas ao ministro do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) Alexandre de Moraes pelo ex-banqueiro do Master, Daniel Vorcaro, agravou a crise de imagem pela qual o Tribunal passa há bastante tempo. E na avaliação do professor de Direito Constitucional e Teoria Geral do Direito na PUC de São Paulo, Pedro Estevam Alves Pinto Serrano, ela nem deveria ter acontecido.


“A retirada do sigilo daquele relatório foi uma decisão ilegal e inusual”

, afirma. “Qualquer magistrado no Brasil, mesmo de primeiro grau, é investigado sigilosamente”, explica.


Professor na PUC-SP, Pedro Serrano defende que ações de ministros do STF tenham consequências


O professor também critica a atitude do ministro André Mendonça em relação à falta de autorização do plenário do STF para iniciar a investigação. Ele lembra que a troca de mensagens entre Vorcaro e Moraes já havia sido divulgada pela imprensa. Portanto, Mendonça “tinha total condição de suspeitar que o ministro Alexandre poderia estar envolvido e uma mera suspeita já enseja pedir autorização pro plenário”.


Por outro lado, mesmo ressaltando que as mensagens não provam nenhuma ilegalidade cometida pelo ministro Alexandre de Moraes, para Serrano, elas trazem “indícios que merecem ser apurados” e, com isso, “caberia uma investigação” da relação de Moraes com o ex-banqueiro.


Alexandre de Moraes também não escapa das críticas do professor quanto ao pedido de investigação contra o colega Mendonça, enviado ao presidente do STF, Edson Fachin, na última quinta-feira, 3 de setembro. “Acho exagerada a decisão de querer investigar o ministro André [Mendonça]. Não acho que esteja caracterizado esse tipo de gravidade na conduta dele. Acho que seria adequado retirá-lo da relatoria”, diz Serrano.


“O ministro André [Mendonça] teve um comportamento inadequado, com relação à própria Corte. E teve também, como foi revelado, uma certa relação com o Vorcaro”, pondera.

A ação, no entanto, não deveria, na visão do constitucionalista, gerar investigação, e sim o afastamento do inquérito, por “fundada suspeita de que ele agiu de forma partidária”.


Entre as medidas apontadas pelo jurista para diminuir o desgaste que o STF já está sofrendo, seria evitar “ficar entrando na lógica do espetáculo”. “Por isso que defendo como uma das medidas que a reunião do plenário do Supremo, para decidir essas questões, só ocorra depois das eleições”.


Dentro dessa lógica do espetáculo, Pedro Serrano cita a proliferação de relatórios da PF nas decisões dos ministros e os vazamentos. “É muito ruim, porque eles são feitos de forma seletiva, e esses relatórios, na maioria das vezes, são ilegais”.


“

O pior é o vazamento de informações; vazar informação é crime. O jornalista que divulga está no exercício do seu direito de informar, natural, inclusive tem direito ao sigilo de fonte. Mas o servidor público, o agente policial, que vaza informação, comete crime.

 Então, o correto seria a polícia cortar na carne, processar quem tem vazado informações”, declara.


Veja os principais trechos da entrevista com o professor:


O STF tem enfrentado crises institucionais, algumas vezes causadas por algum de seus membros, mas em grande parcela geradas por uma campanha difamatória e repleta de desinformação. Qual é o maior risco que a Corte pode sofrer após a retirada do sigilo, pelo ministro André Mendonça, do relatório da Polícia Federal envolvendo o ministro Alexandre de Moraes?


A retirada do sigilo daquele relatório foi uma decisão ilegal e inusual. Qualquer magistrado no Brasil, mesmo magistrado de primeiro grau, é investigado sigilosamente. Não existe nenhum tipo de verificação, apuração que envolva um magistrado que não seja sigiloso.


Isso gera toda uma repercussão pública, a meu ver, prematura e indevida, porque ainda não está claro que foi cometido algum crime. Você tem indícios que ensejam investigar o ministro Alexandre, mas não tem ainda a materialidade do delito. O ministro André Mendonça cometeu um equívoco quando divulgou indevidamente o relatório. E, obviamente, esse equívoco contribui para que haja problemas na imagem do Supremo.


Por outro lado, embora possam querer anular o relatório por conta de investigar um ministro do Supremo, outro equívoco dele foi não ter solicitado autorização do plenário [do STF]. Por mais que ele fale que não tinha como adivinhar que a pessoa [com quem Daniel Vorcaro] estava …

author: Unknown
title: 249 people killed in Syria in eight months
content:
According to information provided by the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights, 249 people (9 women, 92 children and 148 men) have been killed in Syria since the beginning of the year due to explosions of war remnants. Another 388 people were injured.

In other areas under the control of the interim government, 228 people were killed and 368 were injured.

In the regions of North and East Syria, 21 people were killed and 20 were injured as a result of explosions involving war remnants.

author: Andrés
title: Arauco, la forestal, está involucrada en el incendio de 10 casas
content:
Arauco vuelve a atacar en San Pedro. En la provincia de Misiones ostenta la cara violenta del extractivismo forestal. Allí donde tampoco falta la complicidad del gobierno de misiones con la policía, que le cuida las enormes extensiones de tierra a esta multinacional criminal que amenaza a las familias campesinas apropiarse de sus tierras.

Por Clarisa Néztor (ANRed).


Este viernes, Cristian Marcelo Dos Santos no pudo entrar a su casa. Alguien la había incendiado, y el lugar donde había vivido muchos años ya no existía más. Nada quedaba de las paredes, las piezas y todas sus pertenencias. Habían entrado a su chacra de Puerto Argentino 3, y aprovechado su ausencia para incendiarle la casa.


El martes 1° de septiembre la policía había entrado junto a personal de Arauco para exigirle que deje de trabajar su chacra. Lo habían apretado, amenazándolo con 6 meses de cárcel por carpir la tierra, su tierra. Y todo sin mediar orden judicial. El crimen: vivir en su casa, cultivar su tierra, producir lo necesario para la propia subsistencia. Y Cristian, el productor campesino, tuvo miedo. En los últimos  30 días habían incendiado 10 casas de la misma comunidad. Ante el miedo, sacó a sus animales y se llevó algunas pertenencias.


El miércoles pasado, camionetas de Arauco volvieron a recorrer la chacra. Pero este viernes a la tarde, los que vieron el humo proveniente llegaron cuando apenas quedaban unos pilotes en llamas. Demasiado tarde: solo cenizas quedaban de la casa.


Ayer tenía un techo. Hoy ya no. El jueves Cristian Marcelo Dos Santos había cerrado la puerta de un hogar donde se había guarecido de tormentas bravas y veranos voraces. Esta noche no. Tampoco habría puerta que cerrar mañana o el domingo para matear unas horas en el silencio de la tarde.


Y esto que acaba de pasar le sucedió a otras 9 familias el pasado mes. Y volverá a suceder tantas veces como el interés de la clase dominante entre en conflicto con el de la clase desposeída.


Si nos quedamos de brazos cruzados, agarrándonos la cabeza para exclamar “oh, qué horror” y seguir dejándola pasar, no hay chances. Desde que Senadores aprobó la ley de desalojo exprés, y aunque aún no se haya tratado en diputados, ya son 10 las viviendas incendiadas. Y son familias que están perdiendo todo: sus casas, animales, herramientas, cultivos y el lugar donde producen sus alimentos. Vidas truncadas, desarraigadas, desposeídas por políticas mezquinas que le quitan más al débil para acumularlo todo. Familias que sufren amenazas, golpes y criminalización por intentar permanecer en sus territorios.


El despojo territorial en Misiones muestra el entramado mafioso de política, empresa y justicia.


Demandamos al gobierno de Misiones @gobiernodemisiones que Arauco cese inmediatamente el accionar criminal sobre las familias rurales y que se investiguen todos los incendios intencionales denunciados, las amenazas y la participación de la Policía de Misiones en los procedimientos. El gobierno y la justicia está operando en complicidad con la mafia forestal de Arauco.


Defender a las familias también es defender su derecho a la tierra, a producir alimentos y a vivir sin miedo.


Estos son los nombres de quienes se animaron a elevar la denuncia y aparecer públicamente:


Ayala, Julio Martín


Molina, María


Borges, Juan


Antúnez, Diego (presidente de la asoación de colonos unidos por la chacra)


Dos Santos, Cristian Marcelo


Hay otros cinco, que se fueron, que dejaron de pertenecer al grupo por la intimidación sufrida.

author: Nick Reich
title: Fed up with FedEx
content:
On any given day, the FedEx facility in the Melbourne suburb of Tullamarine is a hub of activity, as trucks roar in and out of huge warehouses amid clouds of diesel smoke. On 28 August, something new cut through the routine noise. Just after 8am, hundreds of workers walked off the job, along with thousands of others around the country, costing FedEx millions. As the workers marched defiantly up the driveway, they were met by Transport Workers Union (TWU) officials there with flags to show support.

The previous week, 91 percent of FedEx workers had voted to strike for two hours, after management offered them a previously rejected agreement without any improvements.

The union is asking for an above-inflation pay rise, job security measures that limit AI usage and an end to direct service contracts. FedEx uses these contracts to employ third party drivers without the rights or protections of employees, and they are paid piece rates rather than wages. According to the union, contractors are under pressure to make deliveries every four minutes, which leads to dangerous road conditions not only for the contractors but also for other motorists. Road transport is already the most dangerous industry in Australia—according to the government’s quarterly heavy vehicle road deaths report, in the year to March 2026, 225 people were killed in incidents involving heavy vehicles.

In response to workers voting for a two-hour strike and walking off, FedEx locked them out for the entire day.

I attended their action to show solidarity as a socialist and TWU workplace delegate. Some of the workers I spoke to had been with the company for decades, while for others, this was their first strike. Consistently, the workers expressed anger towards FedEx management, and a keenness to escalate the fight.

“I left Ceva, around the corner, because of bad management” one worker, who was on strike for the first time, told me, “but the same things come up here all the time. Disrespect for the workers”. A longer-term worker said, “I’ve been with this company for 25 years, from when it was TNT to now. It’s always been the same, but especially now this American company thinks they can bring in their model, as if we’re the same as America over here”. The US company, FedEx, bought Australian trucking company TNT in 2016. FedEx has a long history of anti-union practices and undercutting wages. It made more than $4 billion profit last year. 

This strike comes right in the middle of a pivotal year for the TWU’s “Our roads, our skies, our futures” campaign. The day before the FedEx strike, I was at a TWU-run delegates training session. At that, Sam Lynch, lead organiser of the Victorian/Tasmanian branch of the union, explained that a key aim of the campaign is to stop the new operators who are entering the industry in significant numbers from undercutting and driving down workers’ conditions. The union wants to organise workers at these new trucking companies to protect wages and conditions across the industry.

Another is to improve the conditions in unionised companies. To do this, the union is attempting to line up all the major road transport agreements to expire around the same time. Having them all being renegotiated simultaneously opens up the potential for joint, industry-wide industrial action. The union has used this to strengthen its hand at the bargaining table, and the Murdoch press has even run a few stories about the potential chaos an industry-wide strike would cause.

While this all sounds good, the TWU has so far been reluctant to push for the sort of serious industrial action that would be needed to win real gains. Social media posts, press releases and speeches to delegates often labour the point that strikes are a difficult and undesirable last resort. They fail to mention how powerful and unifying strikes can be, especially when they are big enough to cause real problems for the bosses. The TWU leadership have never seriously raised the prospect of industry-wide strikes with members, and they have already signed contracts with two major companies, Linfox and Team Global Express, which weakens the potential for a real industry-wide campaign.

2026 is a key test for the TWU’s strategy, and so far, it isn’t looking like the major surge forward it could have been. There is little advantage that industry-wide bargaining can deliver at the negotiating table if the prospect of industry-wide strikes is so remote that it barely qualifies as …

author: Amanda Audi
title: André Mendonça mobiliza orações e se torna ícone do 7 de setembro bolsonarista
content:
Após a série de atos que estremeceram o Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) nesta semana, o ministro André Mendonça foi alçado ao posto de um dos principais ícones dos evangélicos e um pólo de mobilização para a militância bolsonarista nos atos de 7 de Setembro. Pedidos de oração e abaixo-assinados em apoio ao ministro mobilizaram lideranças políticas e religiosas que apoiam o candidato Flávio Bolsonaro nos últimos dias.


Em posts em redes sociais como X e Instagram, Mendonça é colocado como um contraponto ao ministro Alexandre de Moraes e ao governo Lula. Algumas publicações apresentam a disputa como uma escolha entre dois lados: de um, Lula e Moraes; de outro, Mendonça e o combate à corrupção. Há, inclusive, hashtags de apoio ao ministro, como #EuApoioAndréMendonça.


A “igreja evangélica se une em oração” no episódio descrito como “a maior batalha espiritual das últimas décadas”, diz um texto publicado no portal

Gospel Mais

, que foi replicado em várias outras páginas evangélicas. Um site que coleta assinaturas em apoio ao ministro recebeu mais de 14 mil adesões nas primeiras horas em que esteve no ar.


Pastores e observadores do mundo evangélico relataram à

Agência Pública

 que os pedidos de orações para Mendonça têm sido a forma de adesão mais notável entre grupos cristãos conservadores na véspera de 7 de setembro – o meio costuma ser um dos mais engajados nos atos em apoio ao bolsonarismo.


O pastor presbiteriano e doutor em Sociologia, Valdinei Fernandes, reparou que não tem visto grandes mobilizações de evangélicos para o ato que deve ocorrer no 7 de setembro em São Paulo – programado para ser o maior do dia, com a presença do candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). “O que tem circulado são pedidos de oração pelo ministro André Mendonça”, disse.


O fato de Mendonça ser evangélico ajudou a criar uma aproximação maior com o público – ele é o ministro “terrivelmente evangélico” escolhido por Jair Bolsonaro durante o seu governo. “Mendonça está quase virando um mártir. A extrema direita coloca a situação como se a esquerda estivesse perseguindo um pastor. Não um ministro do Supremo, mas sim um ministro evangélico”, afirma Sérgio Dusilek, pastor batista e teólogo.


No dia em que os novos detalhes do caso Master vieram à tona, 1º de setembro, a dupla sertaneja Zezé di Camargo e Luciano louvou o ministro durante um show em Blumenau, em Santa Catarina. “Vamos pedir uma oração para este homem. Um homem que não tem medo de colocar aquilo que ele crê, aquilo que ele acredita”,

disse

 Luciano, que também relatou que frequenta a Igreja Presbiteriana de Pinheiros, na qual Mendonça é reverendo em São Paulo.


Pastores evangélicos influentes, como o apóstolo Estevam Hernandes, fundador da Igreja Renascer em Cristo e presidente da Marcha para Jesus, e o pastor Silas Malafaia, da Assembleia de Deus Vitória em Cristo, um dos principais mobilizadores de protestos de rua do bolsonarismo, declararam apoio a Mendonça.


“Neste momento, minha oração é para que Deus continue lhe dando sabedoria, coragem e firmeza para cumprir sua missão”, disse Hernandes. Malafaia publicou uma série de vídeos em defesa de Mendonça e com duras críticas a Moraes, discurso que deve ser reproduzido na manifestação programada para a Avenida Paulista, em São Paulo, quando ele prometeu a sua fala “mais dura” contra Moraes.


Políticos bolsonaristas, como os senadores

Magno Malta

 (PL-ES),

Marcos Pontes

 (PL-SP) e

Carlos Viana

 (PSD-MG), também convocaram correntes de oração ao ministro Mendonça. Magno Malta declarou que o magistrado não deve recuar diante de pressões e convocou aliados a fazerem um “clamor de oração” por ele.


Na biblioteca de anúncios do Meta, que congrega conteúdo patrocinado no Instagram e Facebook, há mais de 20 posts impulsionados com pedidos de oração para Mendonça nos últimos dias. A maioria foi paga pelas campanhas de candidatos bolsonaristas.


“Tem um homem em Brasília precisando da oração da igreja hoje”, diz um post de Davi Sacer, cantor gospel e candidato a deputado federal pelo Republicanos por São Paulo, com 1,5 milhão de seguidores. “O ministro André Mendonça está à frente de um dos casos mais importantes do Brasil. (…) Ore com a gente. E compartilha com a sua igreja e o seu grupo de oração: quanto mais gente intercedendo, mais forte essa corrente pelo Brasil.”

title: Dos nuevas querellas contra Luis Hermosilla: tráfico de influencias, cohecho y obstrucción a la justicia en caso Luchsinger Mackay
content:
En la última semana de agosto del 2026, el abogado Luis Hermosilla fue notificado por el 7º Juzgado de Garantía de Santiago de dos querellas en su contra que fueron declaradas admisibles. La primera presentada por José Tralcal Coche y su abogada Karina Riquelme y la segunda presentada por Luis Tralcal Quidel y su abogado Sebastián Saavedra, para investigar su responsabilidad en delitos que impidieron un debido proceso en este mediatizado caso.

“Necesitamos que se rechace la nulidad del caso Luchsinger”, escribió por chat el abogado Luis Hermosilla, entonces Asesor del Ministerio del Interior del Gobierno de Piñera al también abogado y asesor de la cartera José Ramón Correa, actual accionista de Azul Azul. Hermosilla consultó explícitamente por “amigos” en la sala penal que revisaba el recurso de nulidad interpuesto por Luis y José Tralcal, declarados culpables en el caso Luchsinger Mackay, argumentando que “un cuarto juicio sería fatal”. Estos chats revelados por el medio Reportea en junio del 2026, dieron paso a dos querellas presentadas en contra de Hermosilla, declaradas admisibles por el 7º Juzgado de Garantía de Santiago. Desde junio del 2018 José Tralcal Coche, Luis Tralcal Quidel y José Peralino cumplen sentencias por ser declarados culpables de incendio con resultado de muerte en el caso Luchsinger Mackay, cuya principal prueba se basa en una declaración inculpatoria dada por José Peralino Huinca. Quien denunció las torturas que sufrió por parte de los policías para que firmara lo que él calificó como “puras mentiras”. No obstante, el juicio y la condena siguieron adelante, pese a la querella por apremios ilegítimos que Peralino interpuso en contra de los funcionarios de la PDI, la que fue desestimada por el Ministerio Público.

“Todas las pruebas ofrecidas por las defensas que acreditaban la inocencia de los condenados, fueron duramente atacadas por el Ministerio Público, no sólo en estrados, sino también fuera del proceso. Las camareras del motel en que

pasó la noche el día de los hechos Luis Tralcal Quidel, fueron detenidas y el local allanado. Se acusó a los defensores de presentar pruebas falsas y fueron objeto de persecución policial”, señala una editorial del Centro de Investigación y Defensa Sur, CIDSUR publicada en octubre del 2018. Estas son solo algunas de las múltiples irregularidades que organizaciones de derechos humanos han observado en el transcurso de este caso. Para el abogado Sebastián Saavedra, presidente de CIDSUR, “el caso Luchsinger Mackay es un caso clásico de cómo opera la razón de Estado, donde el debido proceso cede frente a las presiones gubernamentales y a los poderes fácticos como son la gente de poder en la región de La Araucanía”.

Cabe recordar que en el Caso Luchsinger Mackay se realizaron tres juicios orales: el primero, en 2014, en contra del Machi Celestino Córdova; el segundo, en 2017, en contra de la Machi Francisca Linconao, Luis Tralcal, José Tralcal y otras ocho personas mapuche; en primera instancia, fueron todos absueltos, pero la sentencia fue anulada por la Corte de Apelaciones de Temuco. Finalmente, en 2018, un tercer juicio oral condenó a Luis Tralcal y José Tralcal a 18 años de cárcel y José Peralino a 5 años de libertad vigilada.

Para el abogado Saavedra, “esta situación es completamente anómala, porque cuando se trata de un comunero mapuche que ha resultado herido o muerto, jamás ha existido este grado de persecución”. Por el contrario, señala que cuando los imputados son personas mapuche, la persecución de los responsables se centra principalmente en los autores materiales, “jamás en personas que hayan planificado o hayan tenido algún otro tipo de participación. Con procesos rápidos y, en su mayoría, penas bajísimas para los autores de los hechos”.

Faltas al debido proceso en el ojo internacional Si se acreditan los delitos de tráfico de influencias por parte de Luis Hermosilla y quienes resulten responsables, las penas llegan hasta los 5 años, lo mismo para el delito de cohecho. En cuanto a la obstrucción a la justicia las penas podrían llegar hasta los 540 días.

Pero más allá de esto, Saavedra señala que, de obtenerse una sentencia condenatoria, “impactaría en la condena que ya ha sido dictada en el caso Luchsinger Mackay, toda vez que implicaría un reconocimiento expreso a la falta de imparcialidad del tribunal y una falta grave al debido proceso y, evidentemente, buscaríamos la anulación de la sentencia”.

title: « Provision commune », kézako ?
content:
Les Provisions communes (il y en a plusieurs en France) partent du postulat que tout le monde doit pouvoir participer à la subsistance = production de biens ou services nécessaires à la vie, et que ces biens et services autoproduits doivent être accessibles à toustes, en mode non-marchand.


T'as dit non-marchand

 

?


Non-marchand, ça veut dire sans la notion d'échange, ni monétaire, ni autre : temps, énergie, compétences… On s'oppose donc résolument à l'idée du mérite qui voudrait que «

 

c'est parce que j'ai jardiné, cuisiné, écrit, réfléchi, tenu une permanence (ou autre…), que j'ai droit à des légumes, un repas, un bocal, une heure de garde d'enfants (ou autre…). On veut ainsi appliquer le principe du communisme radical :

 

»Chacun.e selon ses possibilités, à chacun.e selon ses besoins".


Et concrètement

 

?


Tout ça a l'air bien théorique, mais c'est finalement simple à réaliser (voir une «

 

recette

 

»

ici

, p.29). La Provision commune (

PC

) de Lyon autoproduit sous différentes formes, toujours non-marchandes : fruits et légumes sur un terrain près de Lyon, produits d'hygiène, boissons à base de plantes, préparations fermentées, repas cuisinés, petit livre…, et concernant les services : bientôt entraide administrative, réparation de vélos, garde d'enfants…


À la

PC

 de Lyon, nous voulons que la moitié des productions soit distribuée à l'extérieur de la

PC

, pour visibiliser et faire grandir ce mode de fonctionnement anticapitaliste et non-monétaire. On appelle ça la «

 

PC

 ouverte

 

» et ça se matérialise entre autres sous forme d'un non-marché, où les produits sont à exposés et proposés à toustes.


De la

PC

 au

VC


Une autre forme de

PC

 ouverte s'incarne dans des Vendredis communs (

VC

) qui se déroulent chaque 2

e

 vendredi du mois dans un centre social, et quelquefois en plein air. C'est pendant ces

VC

 que le matin, sont cuisinées les récoltes issues du maraîchage non-marchand, puis à midi, dégustées sous forme d'un déjeuner ouvert à toustes

 

! L'après-midi, il y a le non-marché et une réunion d'orga ou de réflexion. Parallèlement à tout ça, tu peux découvrir des groupes d'autoproduction ou carrément y participer.


C'est où et quand

 

?


Le prochain Vendredi commun, c'est le 11 septembre de 9 à 17h, dans la salle d'un centre social proche d'un métro ligne B.


Puis tous les 2

e

 vendredis du mois : 9/10, 13/11, 11/12..., au même endroit.


Le maraîchage non-marchand, c'est généralement le vendredi après-midi (sauf Vendredi commun, dans ce cas, c'est décalé au dimanche suivant), agenda

ici

. Covoit à partir d'un métro ligne B (eh non, on n'est pas sponsorisé.es par la ligne B lol).


Ça te branche et tu veux en savoir plus : le plus simple, c'est de venir à un

VC

. Sans obligation d'horaire. Juste pour cuisiner, juste pour manger, juste pour jeter un œil ou prendre des infos, tout est possible, on est chô pour faire connaissance et partager notre enthousiasme \o/


Si impossible, eh ben, tu laisses un message

là

… A très vite alors

 

!

title: Memoria Viva de la Fütawillimapu publicará libro sobre la historia y legado de FREDER
content:
“FREDER: Memoria Viva de la Fütawillimapu”, es una iniciativa desarrollada en Osorno que tiene por objetivo difundir los aportes realizados por la histórica Fundación Radio Escuela para el Desarrollo Rural -conocida ampliamente como FREDER- que cuenta con un fundamental trabajo vinculado a la capacitación, educación, comunicación en sectores Mapuche, campesinos y poblacionales urbanos desde los años 60 a la fecha.

Durante 2026, la Corporación de Desarrollo Vertientes, con el apoyo de FREDER y la Fundación Misiones de la Costa, llevará adelante la publicación de un libro titulado “FREDER: Memoria Viva de la Fütawillimapu”. La obra que busca rescatar la memoria, reflexiones y testimonios sobre FREDER, es compilada por el académico Martín Quintana, la psicóloga Marcela Riedemann y la periodista Martina Paillacar, integrantes del equipo del proyecto.

Aborda una amplia diversidad de temáticas, entre ellas el origen de la institución, la identidad del territorio de la Fütawillimapu, la educación y la comunicación, la figura de Winfredo Van den Berg, el rol del cine y el audiovisual. También releva las experiencias de la escuela radiofónica Santa Clara, la trayectoria de Radio La Voz de la Costa, el programa Padres e Hijos y el tradicional Festival del Folclore Campesino de Osorno, entre otros hitos que forman parte de la memoria cultural de la región.

Más de quince autores/as provenientes de la educación, la comunicación y la cultura participan en esta publicación. Entre ellos/as destacan Paula Carrillo, Cristina Añasco, Yamina Mayorga, César Millán, Marcelo Tapia, Fernando Carías Pérez, Cristian Tejeda Gómez, Leonardo Gutiérrez, Hernán Delgado, Ramón Munsón, Ponciano Rumián, Guillermo Williamson y Adrián de Vet. Participan asimismo Martin Quintana, Marcela Riedemann y Martina Paillacar.

En la edición participan el editor José Salomón Gebhard y Mago Editores, mientras que en el diseño y diagramación, participa la ilustradora Catalina Pérez Marrián.

Mujer leyendo una cartilla educativa elaborada por FREDER. Fuente fotografía: FREDER

Asimismo, en la revisión de la publicación, colaboran destacados/as especialistas internacionales y nacionales. Entre ellos/as, Luis Cárcamo-Huchante, académico de la Universidad de Austin-Texas y director de la Native American and Indigenous Studies Association (NAISA), vinculado a estudios indígenas e interculturales; Andrés Tarazona, decano de la Facultad de Educación de la Universidad Agraria de Colombia, experto en educación rural. Se sumaron también las contribuciones de Carmen Gloria Núñez, especialista en educación rural de la Universidad Católica de Valparaíso; el Dr. Guillermo Williamson, de la Universidad de La Frontera, referente en interculturalidad, radio y educación de adultos; e Ignacio Aguaded, catedrático de la Universidad de Huelva, España y director de ALFAMED, asociación internacional de alfabetización mediática.

El libro será distribuido gratuitamente en Osorno y también estará disponible en formato digital. Su lanzamiento está programado para este año, en una actividad abierta a público de todas las edades. Posteriormente, se realizarán mediaciones culturales en centros de salud de Osorno y San Juan de la Costa y la publicación se difundirá en espacios comunitarios, bibliotecas y escuelas, con el propósito de acercar sus contenidos a públicos diversos.

En el marco del proyecto —financiado por el Concurso Nacional Ciencia Pública 2026 del Ministerio de Ciencia, Tecnología, Conocimiento e Innovación— se desarrollará además una página web y se producirán cápsulas radiales que serán transmitidas por Radio La Voz de la Costa, ampliando así el alcance y la difusión de sus contenidos.

Escríbenos al correo: fredercienciapublica@gmail.com

Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/corporacionvertientes

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/rememorias/

author: groundxero
title: Jyotinagar: No Bridge Over ‘Troubled Water’?
content:
Jyotinagar offers a stark glimpse of how access to the most basic necessities can become a weapon against a politically and religiously targeted community.


 


Srijan Dutta


 


It has been 36 days since the municipal tap water supply to the Jyotinagar neighbourhood in the Cossipore area in North Kolkata, was abruptly cut off. The regime change in West Bengal on 4 May promised urban renewal for Kolkata, along with other assurances of growth and development. Kolkatans across classes bought into the prospect of infrastructural revival and societal progress. Among the 5000-odd residents of Jyotinagar Colony, who are all Muslims, many, too, had voted for the BJP. Little did they know that once elected to power, the

Jiska Sath, Uska Vikas

 (Development for only those who support us!) slogan would be enshrined as the ‘double-engine’ government’s guiding philosophy.


 


 


The locality’s inhabitants have now realised that Suvendu Adhikari’s statement was not just mere rhetoric deployed to stir up a pre-election communal cauldron. The KMC pipelines provide treated water through roadside public taps from morning to midnight except for routine outages. This was also the norm for the six public taps at Jyotinagar colony. However, since midnight on 29 July, the taps have remained dry.


 


Nazmul Sheikh, a Jyotinagar youth in his early thirties, explained that this is not another typical case of deferred maintenance on the KMC’s part. He said Ritesh Tiwari, the newly elected BJP MLA from the Kashipur-Belgachia constituency, and his associates had deliberately connived in the scheme to punish the people of Jyotinagar. “We are in this situation because we are poor and Muslims. Our constituency’s new MLA, Ritesh Tiwari has publicly announced swearing on the name of Baba Bholenath that he will not do any work for Muslims in the next five years. We are being deprived of our basic right to access clean water because of his vengeful attitude towards our community”, said Sheikh. He works shifts as a driver at the Cossipore Ghat area. He expressed further anguish over his community’s ordeal stating, “My daily wage is 400 rupees. Since our water supply got suspended, I have been forced to spend around 60-70 rupees every day on drinking water during my work trips.”


Nazmul Sheikh, a Jyotinagar youth and driver, is now forced to spend 60-70 rupees daily on drinking water.


Speaking to Sheikh Mohinuddin, who runs a tea shop and is also the president of CPI(M)-backed Paschim Bangla Basti Unnayan Samiti’s unit at Jyotinagar, made it clearer that the deprivation meted out to them, is not acute but systemic. “We are without water for more than a month. We have formally complained to the municipal authorities on multiple occasions. Each visit ends with shallow sympathetic responses and the responsibility is delegated to some obscure ‘higher authority’. Our union arranges for a municipal water tanker on every alternate day at a charge of 750 to 800 rupees. But that does not suffice everyone.

Bidhayak hoyeche garib manushke dekhar jonno, amader na dekhle kisher jonno sarkar hoeyche…

 (An MLA must look after the poor, if they do not take care of us, what is the government for?)”, stressed Mohinuddin. Furthermore, he mentioned that the electricity connection to the street lights at Jyotinagar had also been disconnected initially. However, the connection was restored after a period of ten days. It was, once again, the logic of communalism that mandated the decision: “Since it was the month of Shraban, this road was bustling with Hindu devotees who had come to fetch water from the Ganges. One of the pilgrims tripped over in the dark. To avoid embarrassment, the authorities quickly reinstated the electricity.”


 


Evening was setting in when I visited Jyotinagar. My conversation with Mohinuddin was interrupted by the sight of women and children coming out from their homes with buckets, pots, bottles, and containers of various shapes and sizes in their hands. Upon enquiry, they told me that they were heading out to collect water for their evening household chores from a nearby public tap. I decided to join them in what I soon learnt has now become their daily quest as I wanted to see the nearest functional tap for myself. To my surprise, the walk was unexpectedly short. An outsider, a journalist or not, might even mistakenly think that it is the same neighbourhood. But we are no longer in Jyotinagar. It is easy to get the wrong impression …

title: ODTÜ'de yol nöbeti: Belediye, iş makinelerini öğrencilerin üzerine sürdü
content:
Ankara Büyükşehir Belediyesinin (ABB) Orta Doğu Teknik Üniversitesi (ODTÜ) arazisindeki Bilkent-İncek bağlantı yolu çalışmalarına karşı öğrencilerin başlattığı nöbet 4 Eylül’de de devam etti. ABB'nin 3 Eylül’de asfalt dökümüne başlaması üzerine çalışma alanına giren öğrenciler iş makinelerinin önünü keserek faaliyetleri durdurdu ve gece boyunca nöbet tuttu.


Eylemin ikinci gününde ABB’ye ait bir araç öğrencilerin üzerine doğru sürüldü. Öğrenciler alanı terk etmedi. Olayla ilgili ABB’den henüz bir açıklama yapılmadı.


Öğrenciler: “Rant yolu”


ODTÜ öğrencileri projeyi “rant yolu” olarak niteliyor. Yeni yolun Ankara’nın trafik sorununu çözmek yerine özel araç kullanımını ve güzergâh üzerindeki yapılaşmayı artıracağını, ODTÜ Ormanı üzerinde yeni ekolojik baskı yaratacağını savunuyor.


Öğrenciler, 2017’de yaklaşık 400 konutluk bir proje çevresinde başlayan yapılaşmanın bugün güzergâh boyunca yaklaşık 12 bin konutluk bir büyüklüğe ulaştığını öne sürüyor. 


ODTÜ Mezunları Derneği ve TMMOB Şehir Plancıları Odası Ankara Şubesi de projeye karşı çıkıyor. Şehir plancıları, yeni karayollarının uzun vadede özel araç kullanımını ve yeni yapılaşmayı teşvik ederek yeniden trafik ürettiğini hatırlatıyor.


Belediye Meclisi 2025’te yeni protokol için yetki verdi


ABB'nin yürüttüğü projenin resmi adı “Bilkent Şehir Hastanesi-İncek Bulvarı-Pozantı Otoyolu Bağlantı Projesi.”


ABB Meclisi'nin 13 Ekim 2025'te oybirliğiyle aldığı kararıyla, proje kapsamında yolun ODTÜ arazisinden geçen bölümü için ABB ile ODTÜ Rektörlüğü arasında yeni bir protokol yapılması öngörüldü ve protokolü imzalamak üzere Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanına yetki verildi.


Öğrencilerin yol çalışmalarının durdurulması ve ODTÜ Ormanı’nı etkileyen kararların üniversite bileşenleri, meslek örgütleri ve Ankara halkının katılımıyla alınması talebiyle başlattıkları nöbet sürüyor. 


Yol mücadelesinin iki perdesi


ODTÜ arazisinin karayolu projeleri için kullanılması ilk kez bugünkü Bilkent-İncek bağlantısıyla gündeme gelmedi.


2013:

 Melih Gökçek yönetimindeki ABB, Anadolu Bulvarı’nı Konya Yolu’na bağlayan yolu ODTÜ arazisinden geçirdi. Ekim 2013’te belediye ekiplerinin gece yerleşkeye girerek ağaçları kaldırması büyük protestolara yol açtı. Yol 2014’te 1071 Malazgirt Bulvarı adıyla açıldı.


2017:

 Bugün tartışılan Bilkent-İncek bağlantı yolu için ABB ile ODTÜ Rektörlüğü arasında bir protokol imzalandı. Eylül 2017’de iş makinelerinin ODTÜ Ormanı’na girmesi yeniden protestolara yol açtı. Gökçek’in aynı yıl görevden ayrılmasının ardından proje tamamlanmadan kaldı.


2021-2026:

 Mansur Yavaş yönetimindeki ABB projeyi yeniden gündeme aldı. ABB Meclisi 2025’te ODTÜ ile yeni protokolün yapılması için belediye yönetimine oybirliğiyle yetki verdi. 3 Eylül 2026’da asfalt çalışmasına başlanması üzerine öğrenciler yeniden nöbete geçti.


Arka Plan |

 Orman kuran ve ormanla kurulan ODTÜ


ODTÜ'nün büyük kent-doğa kompleksinin kampüsü de içeren çok küçük bir bölümü 


ODTÜ Ankara yerleşkesinin üzerinde kurulduğu 4 bin 500 hektarlık alanın yaklaşık 3 bin hektarı orman. ODTÜ arazisinin genişliği, içinde yer aldığı Çankaya ilçesinin toplam yüzölçümünün yaklaşık onda birine karşılık geliyor.Bugünkü ormanın büyük bölümü, üniversiteye 1950’lerde tahsis edilen ve erozyona uğramış Orta Anadolu bozkırının, öğrenciler ve çalışanların da katıldığı yarım yüzyıldır süren bir ağaçlandırma programıyla dönüştürülmesiyle oluştu. 1961’den bu yana milyonlarca ağaç dikildi; yaklaşık 3 bin 100 hektarlık alan 1995’te Doğal ve Arkeolojik SİT olarak ilan edildi.


Ortaya çıkan ormanlık alan yalnızca bir üniversite koruluğundan ibaret değil; Ankara’nın en büyük yeşil alanlarından ve kent içindeki önemli ekosistemlerinden biri. ODTÜ kayıtlarına göre Orman ve Eymir Gölü çevresi, 140’ı aşkın kuş türünün yanı sıra tilki, kurt, tavşan, keklik, sürüngenler ve çeşitli balık türlerine yaşam alanı sağlıyor; ODTÜ'nün büyük yeşil kütlesi, Ankara’nın güneyinde mikroklima üzerinde de etkili. 


Bu doğal çevre, aynı zamanda ODTÜ’nün kuruluşundan itibaren benimsenen kampüs anlayışının bir parçası. Behruz ve Altuğ Çinici’nin 1960’larda geliştirdiği yerleşke planı, eğitim yapıları, yurtlar, sosyal alanlar, yaya yolları ve doğal peyzajıyla tek bir bütün olarak tasarlandı. Yaklaşık 4 bin 500 hektarın yalnızca 800 hektarı yapılaşmaya ayrıldı; geri kalan alan orman, bozkır, arkeolojik miras, rekreasyon ve araştırma alanları olarak korundu. Bu yapı-doğa bütünlüğü dolayısıyla ODTÜ Kampüsü Ağustos 2026’da UNESCO Dünya Mirası …

title: Patron kasasına: 169 milyar TL, beslenme çantasına: 0 TL
content:
Sermayeye yönelik dolaylı ARGE vergi teşvikleri 2024’te 105 milyar 977 milyon TL iken 2025’te 169 milyar 33 milyon TL’ye yükseldi. Teşvikler vergi indirimi yoluyla sağlandı. ARGE teşviki verilen şirketlere toplam 81 milyar TL kurumlar vergisi indirimi, 1.7 milyar TL gelir vergisi indirimi, 140 milyon TL KDV indirimi ve 86.1 milyar TL gelir vergisi stopaj teşviki verildi.

TCMB’nin yıllık ortalama döviz kurlarıyla dolara çevrildiğinde bu artış, şirketlerin cebine giren kaynakta yaklaşık 1 milyar dolarlık bir büyümeye karşılık geliyor. Aynı dönemde milyonlarca yurttaşın yararlandığı sosyal yardım bütçesindeki tablo ise oldukça farklı bir tercihi ortaya koyuyor.

2024 yılında dolar/TL yıllık ortalaması yaklaşık 32.80 TL, 2025 yılında ise yaklaşık 39.46 TL oldu. Bu kurlarla hesaplandığında 2024 yılı dolaylı ARGE teşviki 3 milyar 231 milyon dolardı.

2025 yılı dolaylı ARGE teşviki ise 4 milyar 284 milyon dolara çıktı. Buna göre ARGE teşviki 1 milyar 53 milyon dolar arttı. Bu artışın dağılımı da dikkat çekti. ARGE vergi teşviklerinden yararlanan 11 bin 835 girişimin yüzde 89.5’i KOBİ olmasına karşın, bu girişimler dolaylı ARGE teşviklerinin ancak yüzde 38.2’sini alabildi.

Sayıca toplam girişimlerin sadece yüzde 10.5’ini oluşturan 1243 büyük şirket, dolaylı ARGE teşviklerinin yüzde 61.8’ini kasasına koydu. Buna karşılık, sayıca 10 bin 592 olan KOBİ’nin şirket başına aldığı ortalama teşvik yalnızca 6 milyon 96 bin TL (yaklaşık 154 bin dolar) seviyesinde kaldı. Bir büyük şirket, ortalama bir KOBİ’nin yaklaşık 14 katı oranında vergi teşviki aldı.

Büyük şirketlere sağlanan toplam teşvik tutarı 104.4 milyar TL oldu. 2025 yılı verilerine göre, sistem içindeki büyük ölçekli bir şirket, ARGE vergi teşviki kapsamında ortalama 84 milyon TL destek aldı.

2025 yılında sosyal yardımlara ayrılan toplam kaynak 651 milyar TL, yararlanan kişi sayısı ise 20 milyon idi. Buna göre kişi başına düşen yıllık sosyal yardım tutarı 32 bin 550 TL, aylık tutar ise yalnızca 2 bin 712 TL’de kaldı.

Aynı yıl ARGE vergi teşviklerinden yararlanan 11 bin 835 şirkete dağıtılan 169 milyar 33 milyon TL’yi şirket başına bölündüğünde ise şirket başına yıllık ortalama 14 milyon 282 bin TL’ye varan bir destek ortaya çıktı.

Bir şirkete sağlanan yıllık ortalama ARGE teşviki (14.28 milyon TL), bir yurttaşa verilen yıllık sosyal yardımın (32 bin 550 TL) yaklaşık 438 katı oldu.

TBMM Plan ve Bütçe Komisyonu’nda görüşülen Milli Eğitim Bakanlığının 2025 yılı bütçe görüşmeleri sırasında okullarda öğrencilere bir öğün ücretsiz yemek verilmesine ilişkin toplam 3 önerge de kabul görmemişti. 14 milyon 574 bin öğrenci ye bir öğün yemek verilmesinin yaklaşık maliyeti 165 milyar lira civarındaydı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: ABD'den Türkiye merkezli Golden Global Bank'a yaptırım
content:
Fotoğraf: MohitSingh/Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA 3.0

ABD Hazine Bakanlığı, İran Devrim Muhafızları Ordusu (IRGC) ile bağlantılı olduğu iddiasıyla Türkiye merkezli Golden Global Bank'ı hedef alan yeni yaptırımlar açıkladı.

ABD Hazine Bakanlığı, Golden Global Yatırım Bankası ve bağlantılı kuruluşların, İran'ın Çin'den elde ettiği petrol gelirlerini Türkiye'ye aktarmasına, ardından bu gelirlerin nakit ve altına dönüştürülmesine olanak sağlamak amacıyla kurulduğunu öne sürüyor.

Bakanlık ayrıca bankanın, ABD tarafından daha önce yaptırım uygulananlar da dahil olmak üzere İranlı finans kuruluşlarına bilerek bankacılık hizmetleri sunduğunu iddia etti. Söz konusu İranlı kuruluşlara 2022 yılında, Tahran'ın petrol satışlarından elde ettiği gelirlerin aktarılmasına aracılık ettikleri gerekçesiyle yaptırım uygulanmıştı.

Golden Global, 2019 yılında Türkiye'nin yabancı şirketlere “bankacılık hizmetleri ve alternatif finansman yöntemleri” sunan ilk yatırım bankası olarak kuruldu. İstanbul merkezli banka, internet sitesinde komşu ülkelerdeki hedef pazarlara odaklanarak Türkiye'nin dış ticaretini artırmayı amaçladığını belirtiyor.

Karar sonrası banka, iddiaları reddederek OFAC kararında adı geçen kişi ve kurumların müşterisi olmadığını ve bu kişilerle doğrudan ya da dolaylı hiçbir işlem gerçekleştirmediğini bildirdi.

author: s3nnet.de
title: KDE Plasma 6.8: Verweilklicks
content:
Plasma now features a built-in “dwell clicker” feature! This is an accessibility tool that automatically clicks whenever the pointer is moved somewhere and then left alone for a moment — and what constitutes a “moment” is configurable, of course. It works really well. You can learn a bit more about it on Sebastian’s blog. (Sebastian Sauer, KDE Bugzilla #521391)


Plasma verfügt nun über eine integrierte „Dwell-Clicker“-Funktion (Verweilklicks)! Dabei handelt es sich um ein Barrierefreiheits-Tool, das automatisch klickt, sobald der Mauszeiger an eine Stelle bewegt und dort einen Moment lang ruhen gelassen wird – wobei natürlich konfigurierbar ist, was als „Moment“ gilt. Es funktioniert wirklich gut. Mehr darüber erfahrt ihr in Sebastians Blog. (Sebastian Sauer, KDE Bugzilla #521391)

author: Collin Alexander
title: The power of a hand held: Treaty 6, 150 years later
content:
Chief Edwin Ananas (left), of nîpisîhkopâwiyinînâhk (Beardy’s and Okemasis’ Cree) Nation, holds hands with Governor General Louise Arbour at Treaty 6 commemorations in August.

Photo by Curtis Cameron


For much of this country’s history, Indigenous peoples have been falsely treated by the “Canadian” state as though we need hand-holding. 


A handshake, it seems, was never enough.


Treaty 6 was

negotiated and marked 150 years ago

, first at Fort Carlton, and later at Fort Pitt and at several adhesion sites in the years that followed. (An

adhesion

 was when other communities were later incorporated into an existing treaty).


But it was more than a written legal document; it must be understood through its spirit and intent, grounded in Cree concepts such as pimâtisiwin

(to live a good life),  miyo-wîcêhtowin (to work together), wîtaskêwin (to share the land) — because of wâhkôhtowin (we are all kin).


READ MORE:


‘A living relationship’: Cree Youth honour 150 years of Treaty 6, vowing to carry it forward


Through the Indian Act, the reserve and pass systems, residential schools, and generations of paternalistic policies, “Canada” relentlessly positioned itself as the authority over our lives and nations. 


When Indigenous peoples have asserted our own laws, governance systems, and responsibilities to land and community — under the guidance of Elders — we remind “Canada” that treaties don’t make nations. In fact, it’s nations who make treaties.


Understanding this threatens to unmoor “Canada’s” manufactured power. 


There is an irony in this history: “Canada” assumed the role of guardian, while refusing to recognize Indigenous nations as the capable political partners with whom the Crown had entered treaty — even as “Canada” itself remained tied to the British Crown.


A commemorative medal a Crown representative gave to Cree Chiefs at the signing of Treaty 6 in 1876.

Photo by Curtis Cameron


In 1876, as Treaty 6 was signed, government representatives presented the gathered chiefs with medals. On their face is an image intended to communicate the treaty relationship: a British representative and a First Nations chief stand face-to-face and shake hands. 


Behind them the prairie landscape, with tipis and a rising sun; before them is a pipe (or, as some may see it, a buried hatchet). 


But it’s the handshake that’s at the centre of the scene.


From a European perspective, the handshake was a readily understood symbol of agreement: two men meeting to negotiate, settling terms, concluding a transaction.


Symbolically, a handshake could reduce something as complex as treaty to a single moment — a deal done, hands gripped and then released. 


But in fact, treaty asks that the hands return to one another. 


Treaty must be understood as an enduring, tripartite (three-way) relationship between First Nations peoples, the Crown, and Creator. 


Indigenous peoples bring their nations and their connection with Creator to that relationship; but to honour it, the Crown must also come in good faith to the table.


Earlier this year, a delegation of Treaty 6 chiefs travelled to Buckingham Palace for a private audience with King Charles III.


They requested the Crown return to their territory to honour the treaty’s 150th anniversary. Months later, their invitation was answered: Louise Arbour, the Governor General of Canada, represented the Crown at Fort Carlton. Her presence mattered — not only ceremonially, but as an affirmation of the relationship promised through Treaty 6.


Chief Edwin Ananas (left) and George Stanley (right) hold hands with Governor General Louise Arbour at Treaty 6 commemorations in August.

Photo by Curtis Cameron


On Aug. 23,

exactly 150 years after Treaty 6 was signed

 at Fort Carlton, Arbour stood in between Chief Edwin Ananas — of nîpisîhkopâwiyinînâhk (Beardy’s and Okemasis’ Cree) Nation — and George Stanley, the former chief of Frog Lake First Nation.


Yet rather than simply shaking the governor general’s hand — a gesture so familiar to the imagery of treaty — they held it. 


This handhold asks us to consider whose presence, and what ways of understanding treaty relationships, have been obscured in its visual history. 


Indigenous political life has never existed only within masculine spaces. 


Grandmothers, mothers, matriarchs and women’s societies have always carried law, kinship, language, ceremony, family and responsibilities to future generations. Their roles cannot be …

author: Daron Letts
title: Dog that attacked Iqaluit child dead
content:
The dog suspected to have attacked an 11-year-old

child

 in Iqaluit on Aug. 24 is dead.


It was euthanized on Thursday in the care of the Municipal Enforcement Department, city spokesperson Geoff Byrne announced Friday in a public service announcement.


The attack left the girl with serious injuries to her head and face, and she was later medevaced to Ottawa for surgical treatment.


On Aug. 28, the dog’s owner voluntarily surrendered the animal to bylaw.


“Prior to surrendering the dog, the owner had attempted to arrange for the animal to be euthanized through a veterinary service,” said Byrne in the announcement. “However, this service was not available locally.”


Bylaw officers retained the dog for a 10-day observation period, which was mandated by public health. That observation period ended Thursday.


The investigation into the incident remains ongoing, Byrne said.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Vance Downplays Deadly US Strike on Iranian Wedding: “Things Happen”
content:
He cast doubt on the US’s responsibility for attacking the Iranian wedding party, despite mounting evidence.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Vice President JD Vance cast doubt on and downplayed the U.S.’s strike on a wedding in Iran earlier this week that killed at least four people, despite mounting evidence of U.S. culpability for the civilian killing.

“Sometimes things happen,” Vance said when asked about reports of the strike in a briefing on Thursday.

The strike through the roof of a home in which a wedding was being celebrated in southern Iran on Tuesday killed four people, reports say, including a 4-year-old child, and injured 68 others. Weapons experts and U.S. media reports have said that it was a direct hit to the home with a U.S. munition.

Vance said he’s “extremely skeptical” of the reports of the strike, and that the U.S. “never targets civilians in combat.” But he said that the U.S. is investigating the strike.

“We’re investigating it because obviously we care. We want to know. If we do make mistakes, again, this is a big difference between us and Iran: When our military makes mistakes, they learn from them to try to get better from them,” he said.

However, independent groups have found that the U.S. and Israel killed over 1,700 civilians in Iran between February and April, and have bombed hundreds of civilian sites, including hospitals, schools, and water and electrical infrastructure.

This includes the horrific strike on an elementary school in Minab on the first day of the war that killed 168 people, most of them young children. Trump administration officials also claimed to be investigating that strike, which would be the single most deadly U.S. attack on civilians in decades if verified.

Reuters reported just days after the strike, in March, that an initial investigation found that the U.S. was responsible for the strike. Other reports pointed to the U.S. military recklessly using decades-old targeting data, fed into an AI system, to target the school.

But, as with many such investigations before it, the U.S. has never released the results of the probe, and has never admitted responsibility for the attack. This is despite Vance saying that the U.S. investigates itself in order to avoid future similar incidents.

Indeed, former top State Department human rights official Charles Blaha wrote this week that attacks like the wedding strike are directly downstream of U.S.’s refusal to acknowledge its culpability for the Minab massacre.

“In addition to taking responsibility, DoD should change its targeting procedures to better mitigate the risk of civilian casualties and, ideally, end its illegal war of choice against Iran,” Blaha said. “However, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s opposition to what he calls ‘stupid rules of engagement’ suggests that pressure for any changes designed to protect civilians in war must come from outside DoD.”

Vance’s comments are the latest instance of the Trump administration callously dismissing its violence against civilians on its various war fronts. In July, Trump said that he doesn’t believe “anyone’s ever going to be able to say what happened” in Minab — and went even further by falsely suggesting that images of the massacre were “AI-generated.”

Truthout is funded almost entirely by readers — that’s why we can speak truth to power and cut against the mainstream narrative. But independent journalists at Truthout face mounting political repression under Trump.

author: The Canadian Press
title: Innu Nation grand chief calls for Indigenous police force after violent N.L. arrest
content:
The grand chief of the

Innu Nation

 says the violent arrest of an Indigenous man in Labrador caught on camera highlights the need for a First Nation-led police force in the region.


Jodie Ashini said a video posted on social media on Wednesday of three RCMP officers arresting the man in the Sheshatshiu Innu First Nation, a community of 1,300 about 30 kilometres north of Happy Valley-Goose Bay, was difficult to watch. It appears to show one officer repeatedly punching the man in the head before triggering a stun gun several times.


She said the video shows officers using excessive force.


“He had three people on him,” Ashini said in an interview Thursday. “He was getting punched repeatedly.”


The video, which has been shared online thousands of times, appears to show three RCMP officers in the process of arresting a man inside a home. When the man appears to pull his hand back from police, one of the officers punches him in the face.


The video also appears to show the man being thrown against a wall, punched again, taken to the ground, and punched several more times before an officer appears to hit him multiple times with a stun gun.


“It was too much,” Ashini said. “It was just beyond anything that any RCMP member should ever do to somebody.”


At one point, an officer appears to push the woman filming, who says the man being arrested is her boyfriend. The officer says the arrested man had spit in an officer’s face. A barking dog and people screaming can be heard throughout the incident and at least one child can be seen on the fringes of the video.


An RCMP spokesperson declined to offer more information about the Sheshatshiu incident on Thursday, saying it had been referred to the Serious Incident Response Team, the province’s civilian-led oversight agency for police.


The Mounties said they met with Ashini, Sheshatshiu Chief Eugene Hart and other community leaders Wednesday.


“We will continue to engage directly with the community in these important conversations,” said the statement.


Ashini said RCMP officials told her that the officer seen throwing punches in the video has temporarily been reassigned to Happy Valley-Goose Bay. She said that’s not enough disciplinary action and the officer should have been suspended.


“He’s still going to have interactions in Goose Bay with other people. And it’s just a scary thought of him with any other Indigenous person,” she said.


Ashini said the incident illustrates why the Innu people need their own police force.


The issue has been part of the Innu Nation’s land claim and self-governance negotiations with the federal and provincial governments that have been going on for more than 40 years, she added.


As it stands, Ashini said the Innu can’t access federal funding for its own police force.


“We grew up in the same traumatic way (and) we understand each other,” said Ashini. “There are ways that we can talk to our own people, to bring people down, rather than using force, using intimidation, using these techniques that the RCMP is known for.”


As of 2024, there were 36 First Nation and Inuit-led police services serving 157 communities across the country, according to Public Safety Canada.


The Innu Nation is not the only Indigenous group seeking its own police service. In January, the chief of New Brunswick’s Neqotkuk First Nation called for the establishment of its own force after RCMP shot and killed community member Paul Bronson during a domestic call. He was the fourth Indigenous person killed by police in New Brunswick since 2020.


That same month, an RCMP officer shot and killed a man from Sipekne’katik First Nation in Nova Scotia along a highway north of Halifax. The two deaths prompted First Nation chiefs across Atlantic Canada to call for an urgent meeting with the federal government.


Read more:


 


Innu Nation rejects apology from N.L. government that doesn’t mention 300-year history cap


Deaths of 6 Innu youth rooted in ‘colonial legacies’ and service gaps say investigators at Innu inquiry


In July, the Serious Incident Response Team overseeing Nova Scotia and New Brunswick added an Indigenous investigator after years of advocacy from First Nations. Earlier this year, New Brunswick’s Indigenous Affairs Minister Keith Chiasson said early talks on an Indigenous-led public inquiry into systemic racism were underway.

author: CMI Argentina
title: “Galtierazo” y “admiración por Thatcher”: ex combatientes de Malvinas responden a la cadena de Milei
content:
Desde el Cecim salieron a cuestionar el discurso del presidente. Recordaron su valoración por Thatcher y lo compararon con un episodio de Galtieri. Además, marcaron las contradicciones de los anuncios sobre Malvinas.


Unas horas después de la cadena nacional a cargo de Javier Milei, ex combatientes de Malvinas analizaron el discurso y cuestionaron al Presidente pese a que remarcó el reclamo de soberanía sobre las islas. Desde el Cecim, por caso, marcaron al episodio como un “Galtierazo” y además señalaron que se fundamenta en la admiración del líder de La Libertad Avanza por Margaret Thatcher. “Es la mayor expresión de hipocresía del Presidente y su gabinete”, dijo Rodolfo Carrizo, titular de esta organización, en diálogo radial.


En comunicación con

FutuRöck

, Carrizo señaló que “el discurso de ayer se explica con su admiración por Margaret Thatcher” y agregó: “Creo que a Estados Unidos siempre le interesó Malvinas. Es un lugar ultra estratégico y lleno de riquezas naturales”.


“El discurso de ayer se explica con su admiración por Margareth Thatcher. Es la mayor expresión de hipocresía del Presidente y su gabinete”


 Rodolfo Carrizo, excombatiente y presidente del CECIM en

#TotalNormalidad

September 4, 2026


¿Un reclamo impostado por Malvinas?


En tanto, Jerónimo Guerrero Iraola, abogado del CECIM, también evaluó la presentación de una medida cautelar para frenar el proyecto petrolero “Sea Lion” en Malvinas. “Nosotros lo caracterizamos como un Galtierazo”, describió en comunicación con la radio de La Voz de Córdoba y marcó un paralelo con la historia argentina.


A su vez, el abogado remarcó que el discurso se choca con las políticas que llevó adelante La Libertad Avanza durante su gestión, entre otras contradicciones. “Busca un endurecimiento de penas, sobre una ley que ya existe y sobre la que el Gobierno no ha echado mano. La ley que Milei dijo querer reformular es la ley vigente y cuando habló de perseguir a quienes brinden apoyo logístico ya está previsto en las normativos, incluso con penas muy duras”, evaluó.


La cadena de Milei


Este jueves, Milei anunció sanciones para las empresas petroleras que operen en las Islas Malvinas y la construcción de una base militar en Tierra del Fuego. Dijo que el gobierno endurecerá las sanciones y penas para compañías que actúen en el archipiélago, las que no podrán trabajar en la Argentina y se expondrán a un juicio en ausencia. Sin embargo, las firmas petroleras

Rockhopper Exploration, de Gran Bretaña, y Navitas Petroleum

, de Israel, que llevan adelante la búsqueda de petróleo bajo el mar al norte de las islas Malvinas nunca fueron castigadas por este gobierno.

title: ᓱᕈᓯᖅ ᑐᐊᕕᕐᓇᖅᑐᒃᑯᑦ ᖃᖓᑕᓲᒃᑯᑦ ᐊᐅᓪᓚᖅᑎᑕᐅᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᕿᒻᒥᒧᑦ ᐹᔭᐅᓚᐅᖅᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᐃᖃᓗᖕᓂ
content:
For the English version of this story, please see

Child medevaced after dog attack in Iqaluit

.


ᓄᓇᓕᐸᐅᔭᖅ ᐃᖃᓗᖕᓂ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᐳᖅ ᕿᒻᒥᒧᑦ ᐹᔭᐅᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐋᒍᔅᑎ 24−ᒥ ᕿᒪᐃᓚᐅᖅᑐᒥ 11-ᓂ−ᐅᑭᐅᓕᖕᒥ ᓂᕕᐊᖅᓵᒥᒃ ᐋᓐᓂᕐᓂᕐᔪᐊᖑᔪᓂ ᓂᐊᖁᖓᒍᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑮᓇᖓᒍᑦ.


ᒦᐊ ᔪᐊᐃ ᓇᐅᓪᓚᖅ−ᕗᕋᐃᓱᕐ ᐹᖅᓯᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᕿᒻᒥᒥᒃ ᐃᒡᓗᐃᑦ ᕿᑎᐊᒎᖅᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᑕᐅᓇᓂ ᓄᓇᓕᖕᓂ ᓄᓇᓕᐸᐅᔭᒥ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐊᓈᓇᖓ  ᑲᓕ ᓇᐅᓪᓚᖅ.


ᐸᖅᑭᔭᐅᓂᖃᓚᐅᖅᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᐃᖃᓗᖕᓂ,  ᓇᐅᓪᓚᖅ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐸᓂᖓ ᑐᐊᕕᕐᓇᖅᑐᒃᑯᑦ ᖃᖓᑕᓲᒃᑯᑦ ᐊᐅᓪᓚᖅᑎᑕᐅᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐋᑐᕚᒧᑦ 8 ᐅᓐᓄᒃᑯᑦ ᐅᖓᑎᑦᑎᐊᖓᓂ ᐋᒍᔅᑎ 25−ᒥ.


“ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑕᐅᔭᕆᐊᖃᕐᒪᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᓗᓂ ᐱᓚᒃᑐᐃᔨᒧᑦ ᐋᓐᓂᕐᓂᐅᔪᓄᑦ ᐃᔨᐅᑉ ᖄᖓᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐅᕕᓂᖃᙱᓐᓂᐅᔪᒥ,”  ᓇᐅᓪᓚᖅ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᕙᐃᔅᐳᒃᑯᑦ ᐅᖃᖃᑎᖃᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ, ᒪᕐᕉᒃ ᐃᑭᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ ᖃᖓᑕᓲᒧᑦ. “ᐱᓚᒃᑐᐃᔨ ᐃᓱᒪᓕᐅᕆᓂᐊᖅᐳᖅ ᐋᖅᑭᒃᓱᖅᑕᐅᒃᑲᓐᓂᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐃᓅᓕᓴᖅᑕᐅᔭᕆᐊᖃᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ, ᐃᓚᖃᖅᑐᒥ ᐅᕕᓂᖓᓂ ᑲᑎᑕᐅᔪᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᔨᖓᑕ ᖄᖓᓂ ᐋᖅᑭᒃᑕᐅᓂᖓᓄᑦ.”


ᕿᒻᒥᖅ ᐃᒡᓘᑉ ᑐᓄᐊᓃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᑕᐃᔅᓱᒪᓂ ᐹᔭᐅᓂᐅᓂᐊᖅᑐᒥ,  ᓇᐅᓪᓚᖅ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


ᓇᐅᓪᓚᖅ ᑎᑎᕋᖅᓯᒪᕗᖅ ᐃᓅᖃᑎᒌᖑᔪᓄᑦ ᓯᐊᒻᒪᖅᑎᑦᑎᕝᕕᐅᔪᒥ ᖃᓄᐃᓐᓂᐅᓚᐅᖅᑐᒥ, ᐅᖃᐅᓯᐅᕈᓘᔭᖅᓯᒪᔪᒥ ᓄᓇᕗᓕᒫᒥ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᖃᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐃᓱᒫᓘᑕᐅᔪᓂ ᕿᒻᒥᓂᒃ ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᓂᕐᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᓄᓕᒫᓂᒃ ᐊᑦᑕᓇᔾᔭᐃᖅᓯᓯᒪᓂᕐᒥ.


“ᐊᖏᓛᖑᔪᒥ ᐃᓱᒫᓘᑎᒋᔭᕋ ᓇᓗᓇᐃᖅᓯᓂᕐᒥ ᖃᓄᐃᓐᓂᐅᓚᐅᖅᑐᒥ ᐸᓂᓐᓄᑦ ᐃᓱᒪᒋᔭᐅᑦᑎᐊᕐᓂᖓᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐊᓯᐊᓂ ᐃᓄᖕᒥ ᓱᕈᓯᕐᒥᓪᓘᓐᓃᑦ ᐋᓐᓂᖅᑐᖃᒃᑲᓐᓂᙱᒃᑯᓂ,”  ᓇᐅᓪᓚᖅ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


ᓄᓇᓕᐸᐅᔭᖅ ᐃᖃᓗᖕᓂ ᐃᓄᓕᒫᓄᑦ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᕐᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᒃᓴᓕᐅᓚᐅᖅᐳᑦ ᐋᒍᔅᑎ 25−ᒥ ᖃᓄᐃᓐᓂᐅᔪᒥ, ᐅᖃᖅᖢᑎᒃ ᓄᓇᓕᐸᐅᔭᖅ ᐃᓕᓴᖅᓯᓂᖓᓂ “ᐱᓪᓚᕆᐅᔪᒥ ᐃᓱᒫᓘᑕᐅᔪᒥ” ᓄᓇᓕᐅᑉ ᐃᓗᐊᓂ ᒪᓕᒃᑐᒥ ᐹᔭᐅᓂᐅᔪᒥ.


ᕿᒻᒥᖃᖅᑎᐅᔪᑦ ᑲᒪᒋᔭᖃᖅᐳᑦ ᓇᓗᓇᐃᖅᓯᓂᕐᒥ ᑎᒍᐊᖏᑦ ᐅᒋᐊᖅᓯᙱᓐᓂᖏᓐᓂ ᐅᕝᕙᓘᓐᓃᑦ ᐋᓐᓂᖅᓯᓗᑎᒃ ᐊᓯᖏᓐᓂ, ᐅᕝᕙᓘᓐᓃᑦ ᓱᔪᐃᓗᑎᒃ ᐱᖁᑎᒋᔭᐅᔪᓂ, ᐅᖃᐅᓯᐅᓪᓗᓂ ᓄᓇᓕᐸᐅᔭᖅ ᐃᖃᓗᖕᓂ ᐆᒪᔪᓄᑦ ᐊᐅᒪᑕᐅᓂᖏᓐᓄᑦ ᒪᓕᒐᕋᓛᖑᔪᒥ. ᐸᖅᑭᔭᐅᑦᑎᐊᕋᓗᐊᖅᐸᑕ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᑦᑎᐊᕐᒪᖔᑕ ᕿᒻᒥᖓᓂ, ᕿᒻᒥᖃᖅᑎᐅᔪᑦ “ᐸᓯᔭᒃᓴᐅᕗᑦ ᐱᕋᔭᖕᓂᐅᔪᒥ” ᕿᒻᒥᖅ “ᐹᒋᐊᕈᓂ, ᑲᑉᐱᐊᓵᕆᓗᓂ ᐅᕝᕙᓘᓐᓃᑦ ᐋᓐᓂᖅᓯᒍᓂ ᐃᓄᖕᒥ.”


ᒪᐃᔭᐅᑉ ᑐᖓᓕᖓ ᑭᒻᐳᓕ ᓯᒥᑦ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᖃᓄᐃᓐᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᑕᐃᑲᓂ ᐋᒍᔅᑎ 25−ᒥ ᓄᓇᓕᐸᐅᔭᒃᑯᑦ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᓄᑦ ᑲᑎᒪᓂᐅᔪᒥ, ᐅᖃᖅᖢᓂ ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᑦ ᐅᖃᑎᖃᖅᓯᒪᕗᑦ ᐃᓚᒌᖑᔪᓄᑦ.


ᓯᕗᓪᓕᕐᒥ, ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᑦ ᓯᕗᓪᓕᐅᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑎᐅᓂᕐᒥ, ᓄᓇᓕᖕᓂ ᒪᓕᒐᕋᓛᓕᕆᔨᓂ ᑐᓂᓯᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᐃᑲᔪᖅᓱᐃᓂᕐᒥᑦ.


ᓄᓇᑦᓯᐊᖅ ᑐᓴᒐᒃᓴᓕᕆᔨᒃᑯᑦ ᐃᓴᒃᓯᒪᕗᑦ ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᓐᓄᑦ ᐊᐱᕆᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᖃᓄᐃᒻᒪᑦ ᐃᓇᖏᖅᓯᓚᐅᕐᓂᖏᓐᓂ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᑭᓯᐊᓂ ᑭᐅᔭᐅᓂᖃᓚᐅᙱᓚᑦ ᐆᒧᖓ ᐊᐱᖅᑯᑕᐅᔪᒧᑦ.


ᑭᓯᐊᓂ, ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᑦ ᐅᖃᖅᑎᖓ Cpl. ᐋᔅᓕ ᑕᐃᓕ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᑦ ᓇᓗᓇᐃᖅᓯᓯᒪᕗᑦ ᕿᒻᒥᒥᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᕿᒻᒥᖃᖅᑎᐅᔪᒥ.


ᐋᒍᔅᑎ 26−ᒥ, ᓄᓇᓕᐸᐅᔭᖅ ᐅᖃᖅᑎᖓ ᔨᐊᕝ ᐱᐅᓐ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᑐᓴᒐᒃᓴᓕᐊᖑᔪᒥ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑕᐅᓂᖓ ᐅᑎᖅᑎᑕᐅᕗᖅ ᓄᓇᓕᐸᐅᔭᒃᑯᓐᓄᑦ ᐃᓚᖃᙱᒻᒪᑦ ᐱᕋᔭᖕᓂ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ.


“ᑐᙵᕕᖃᖅᑐᒥ ᑐᓴᒐᒃᓴᓕᐊᓂ ᑲᑎᖅᓱᖅᑕᐅᔪᓂ ᑕᐃᑲᓂ [ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᑦ] ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑕᐅᓂᖓᓂ, ᕿᒻᒥᖅ ᐃᐲᙶᓚᐅᙱᓚᖅ ᑕᐃᔅᓱᒪᓂ ᖃᓄᐃᓐᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᐅᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐃᐱᖅᓯᒪᓂᖓᓂ,” ᐱᐅᓐ ᑎᑎᕋᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᑦ ᓱᓕ ᑐᓂᓯᔭᕆᐊᖃᖅᐳᑦ ᑎᑎᖅᑲᖁᑎᖏᓐᓂ ᓄᓇᓕᐸᐅᔭᐅᑉ ᒪᓕᒐᕋᓛᓕᕆᔨᒃᑯᓐᓄᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᕝᕕᖓᓄᑦ. ᐱᓕᕆᕝᕕᐅᑉ ᕿᒥᕐᕈᔭᐅᓂᖓ ᐱᔭᕇᖅᐸᑦ, ᓄᓇᓕᐸᐅᔭᖅ ᑐᓂᓯᓂᐊᖅᐳᖅ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᖓᓕᕐᓂᖓᓂ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


“ᓄᓇᓕᐸᐅᔭᖅ ᐃᓕᓴᖅᓯᕗᖅ ᐱᓪᓚᕆᐅᓂᖓᓂ ᐆᒪᙵᑦ ᖃᓄᐃᓐᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᓱᒫᓘᑕᐅᔪᒥ ᐱᑎᑦᑎᓂᖓᓂ,” ᐱᐅᓐ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


ᒪᓐᓇᒧᑦ ᑎᑭᖦᖢᒍ ᒪᓕᒐᕋᓛᓕᕆᔨᒃᑯᑦ ᑭᐅᓯᒪᕗᑦ 17−ᓄᑦ ᕿᒻᒥᓄᑦ ᖃᓄᐃᓐᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ 7−ᓂ ᐆᒪᔪᓂ ᐱᑦᑎᐊᙱᕐᔪᐊᕐᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᐅᖃᐱᓘᑕᐅᔪᓂ. ᓄᓇᓕᐸᐅᔭᖅ 9−ᓂ ᕿᒻᒥᓂᑦ ᑐᖂᑦᑎᓯᒪᕗᑦ.

title: Protest against geothermal power plant project ends 124th day
content:
The vigil launched by the Youth Assembly of the Gimgim (Varto) Ecology Platform against the Geothermal Power Plant (JES) project in Xwarik village is ongoing.


A banner reading “The people of Varto do not want a geothermal power plant. Do not touch my water, my soil” was hung at the vigil site as the protest entered its 124th day.


Visiting the vigil site, New Party Istanbul MP Evrim Rızvanoğlu said the concerns of the people of Gimgim regarding the project were justified. Rızvanoğlu also criticised the decision that an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) was “not required” for the project.


Gimgim Ecology Platform member Çayan Dursun said the struggle against the geothermal power plant project had been ongoing since January 22, and that the tent vigil had continued since May 3.


Dursun said they were also pursuing the struggle through legal channels and stressed the importance of bringing the issue before Parliament. “We will win; there is no second option. We do not accept anything carried out without the consent of the people,” he said.


Following the statements, the delegation met with citizens maintaining the tent vigil and exchanged views on the process.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Entre Ríos: ya son 480 los despedidos en Granja Tres Arroyos de Concepción del Uruguay
content:
Entre el 1 y el 3 de septiembre 210 trabajadores más recibieron el telegrama de despido, con lo que suman un total de 480 operarios de la planta “La China”  que fueron despedidos arbitrariamente.


Escuchá el reporte de Adriana Defazy desde Radio Sapukay.


El día miércoles algunos de los trabajadores decidieron encadenarse frente al Municipio para exigir respuesta del estado ante una situación desesperante de casi 950 familias que son víctimas de que la industria cierre su fuente de trabajo.


Maximiliano Zalazar es delegado y trabajador de La China, este miércoles 2 realizaron una concentración frente al Municipio de la ciudad de Concepción del Uruguay, para exigir respuestas y acompañamiento: “Tuvimos un acercamiento del intendente José Eduardo Lauritto que vino a dialogar, a hablar con nosotros. Lo que nos promete es poder llegar a un diálogo, a una reunión con Joaquín de Gracia, o con Marcelo de Gracia, que son los dueños de la empresa”.


Lo que nosotros exigimos es la reapertura de la empresa, la reapertura de la fábrica, que vuelvan a tomar nuevamente a los compañeros despedidos, que los que no están despedidos reingresen a trabajar nuevamente, y que a quienes ya no quieren volver a ingresar, se les pague debidamente su indemnización, como corresponde”, aseguró el delegado.


Le deben a todos los trabajadores desde la segunda quincena de abril, los salarios de mayo, junio, julio y agosto, y el aguinaldo. La falta de pagos afectó tanto a los empleados desvinculados como a quienes continuaron integrando la plantilla. Estos 480  despidos se suman a 1.000 trabajadores en sus plantas bonaerenses de Capitán Sarmiento, Esteban Echeverría y Pilar.

author: Chris Walker
title: Missouri Supreme Court Blocks GOP Maps, Puts Gerrymandering Issue to Voters
content:
The decision will likely be appealed by Republican state leaders to the US Supreme Court.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Missouri voters will be given the chance to weigh in on maps redrawn by the Republican-led state legislature last year, which created congressional boundaries many critics have said are both racial and political gerrymanders.

In a unanimous ruling on Thursday, the Missouri Supreme Court found that a “veto referendum” ballot initiative was unduly blocked by Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins (R).

In 2025, as part of President Donald Trump’s push for Republican-led states to gerrymander congressional districts for political gain in the 2026 midterms, Missouri lawmakers split up a district in Kansas City, dividing the municipality into three other districts and diluting the Black vote in the area. The resulting maps meant that it was likely Republicans would gain a seat in Congress, while Democrats would lose one.

In response, a nonprofit group called People Not Politicians Missouri organized and gathered more than 300,000 signatures statewide to veto the law, sometimes referred to as HB 1. After the group submitted their signatures in December, Hoskins waited for the longest possible time permitted to him under state law to block the initiative, doing so in early August by deeming the measure unconstitutional, arguing that such ballot measures couldn’t be used to block redistricting bills.

People Not Politicians Missouri sued over the move. After a lower state court ruled in favor of Hoskins, the case went on to the Missouri Supreme Court, which heard arguments this week on the matter.

The state’s highest court disagreed with Hoskins’s interpretation of the state constitution.

“The plain language of Article III, Section 49 of the Missouri Constitution authorizes a referendum as to ‘any act of the general assembly,'” the court’s ruling stated, noting that “no exception applies,” making the petition by People Not Politicians Missouri “legal, sufficient, and timely.”

The Missouri Supreme Court determined that the measure must be put on November’s ballot. Furthermore, the court ruled that “HB 1 never took effect” due to state rules blocking measures from being implemented if they’re challenged by veto referenda.

The ruling means that the gerrymandered maps will be blocked, for now, with the state reverting to maps drawn after the last census for the fall races.

The Missouri Supreme Court’s decision will be appealed by Republican state lawmakers, who will likely argue that, because primary elections have already occurred using the new maps, the state cannot revert to the older boundaries.

Because the state’s highest court ruled on the matter, the only appellate option available is the U.S. Supreme Court.

“Our office will move immediately to seek relief from SCOTUS,” Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway (R) said on X.

Still, advocates for the veto ballot measure praised the ruling.

“This is what democracy looks like,” said Richard von Glahn, executive director of People Not Politicians Missouri. “The people of Missouri demanded a voice, and the court just confirmed what we’ve been saying all along: People, not politicians, will have the final say.”

author: Elinor Epperson
title: Resistance Grows Against MI Data Center That Would Fuel Nuclear Weapons Research
content:
Residents are concerned that the joint University of Michigan/Los Alamos facility will power a nuclear arms race.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The University of Michigan’s proposed computing facility in Ypsilanti Township is the next step in high-powered computing and nuclear weapons research for Los Alamos National Laboratory. Nonproliferation experts say the research could also contribute to the development of new weapons.

The $1.2 billion research center would be almost 300,000 square feet, with the lion’s share going to Los Alamos. A much smaller portion – about 50,000 square feet – would go to the university for nonclassified research. First announced in 2024, the project has drawn opposition from residents and the township as commercial data centers pop up across Michigan.

The university argues that while the facility resembles a commercial data center, its purpose is quite different. The project would use high-powered computing to perform scientific experiments and support research across a variety of disciplines – including nuclear weapons research for the U.S.’s Stockpile Stewardship Program.

That has drawn further criticism and concern from residents, officials, and members of the university community – who argue that research goes beyond maintaining the U.S.’s existing stockpile.

None of this work is new to Los Alamos, which has been running these experiments for decades. Started in the mid-1990s, the program uses physical experiments and computer simulations to explore how nuclear weapons behave and perform – without live detonations.

Those computer simulations capture data for processes that happen in slivers of a second. That could be the simulated detonation of a nuclear weapon, or something more mundane like materials science, how the nuclear fuel decays, fluid dynamics, and more.

The U.S. uses data gleaned from this research to maintain its stockpile of about 3,700 nuclear weapons.

Los Alamos and other national labs have steadily increased their computing power as their research needs and computing technology evolve.

It’s not unusual for Los Alamos to collaborate with the University of Michigan, said Dylan Spaulding, senior scientist at the Global Security Program at the Union of Concerned Scientists.

“There is a long history of collaboration between universities and the Department of Energy or the National Nuclear Security Administration, as well as Department of Defense,” he said.

Steve Ceccio, the project lead for the proposed facility, said the decades-long collaboration has benefited both institutions and high-powered computing research.

“They are at the bleeding edge of this. And so our researchers, their people, we work together to sort of push the envelope,” he said. “That’s why Michigan and Los Alamos’s partnership is so important to us, because it really is helping us advance the field.”

What’s unusual is the amount of classified research the facility could be doing, Spaulding said.

“What appears to separate this collaboration may be the level of classification attached to this new data center,” he said. Handling classified information “suggests that it may be sort of taking a more aggressive approach towards weapons-related science than fundamental science that you would find in the open literature.”

The facility would be doing nonclassified research as well, Ceccio said, noting that researchers from a wide variety of disciplines could propose using the university’s side for their needs. Los Alamos has used its computing systems to model wildfire behavior and study changes in Arctic sea ice, according to the university.

But it’s unclear how much of the facility’s resources would be devoted to national security research, and how much would go to fundamental research. The university and Los Alamos referred most specific questions about the facility to each other. While Michigan Advance gave Los Alamos several weeks to arrange an interview, no one from the organization was available to comment.

The primary purpose of the Ypsilanti facility would be to continue the classified work Los Alamos has already been doing, including research on nuclear weapons, Ceccio said.

“They would be using that facility to advance their basic mission for national security,” he said.
